_about: Demo tour of the verified quicksort. Sources: verification/catalogue/pages/quicksort.md (its sources: list is the backbone), research/mastery-20260927/borrowing.md (prophecies, the borrow transitions in vox_vc.ml, the soundness argument), design-docs/borrows-and-slices.md. The mastery report describes an older parallel sort (a runner abstraction over Slice.parallel on borrowed slices); HEAD sorts owned arrays with Vox_parallel.fork_join, and this tour follows the code at HEAD (8479634adc). Build status: without --enable-multidomain, runtime/caml/domain.h sets Max_domains to 1, so Domain.recommended_domain_count () is 1 (runtime/domain.c). Name-keyed borrow facts: at 8479634adc normal_borrow_transition applies to any external with a caml_borrow_* C name; trunk a187b9ab9c (merge of trust-hardening, commit 9864700994) restricts built-in meanings to the owning library's declarations. Stop 8 states only what holds at both revisions. Stops 5, 6 and 8 omit 'lines'. Borrowing was made partial on 28 September 2026 (branch jujacobs/vox/partial-borrows-20260928): the borrowing sort is no longer total, and sort_array sorts owned arrays without loans.
title: Quicksort: borrowed slices and a plain fork/join
summary: `Quicksort` sorts a mutable `int` array in place and is proved to leave it sorted and a permutation of its input. The borrowing sort works on uniquely borrowed slices whose contract is stated with a prophecy, `Borrow.Slice.final`, the contents a slice will have when its borrow ends; it is not total, because creating and ending a loan are not. The total sort and the parallel sort split an owned array into disjoint owned pieces; the parallel sort sorts two of them with `Vox_parallel.fork_join`, whose type is ordinary polymorphism: the proofs come back through the join as refined type arguments.

The tour goes from the interface and the slice library to the three recursions, then to what the checker assumes about borrows and what it checks about erasure. The [catalogue page](demo:quicksort) states the claim, the trusted base and the scope.

stops.title: The interface: three sorts, one of them total
stops.from: val sort : (s : int Borrow.Slice.t) @ local unique ->
stops.text: `sort` takes a slice `@ local unique`: the caller lends its only reference, and the slice cannot escape the call. Its contract relates two erased views of the slice, `Borrow.Slice.current s`, the contents at the call, and `Borrow.Slice.final s`, the contents when the borrow ends. `sort_array` and `parallel_sort_array` consume an owned array and return one, and state the same property on `Borrow.Owned_array.contents`; `Spec` is `Vox_int_sequence`. Only `sort_array` is `@@ total`: `sort` creates and ends loans, which are not total operations, and `parallel_sort_array` starts domains. Their contracts hold on normal return only, and if `parallel_sort_array` raises the array is lost.

stops.title: A slice carries a prophecy
stops.to: && final r === final s} @ local unique @@ total
stops.text: `current` and `final` are ghost externals, which exist for the checker only; `Slice.set` consumes the slice and returns a successor whose `current` is updated and whose `final` is unchanged, so a borrow's history is a chain of handles that share one prophecy. `Slice.finish`, further down, resolves it: its result is `{u : unit | final s === current s}`. `Owned_array.with_mut` lends an owner as a slice and, when the callback returns, sets the owner's `contents` to that slice's `final`. `set` is `total`, but the operations that create a loan (`with_mut`, `split_at`, `split3`, `with_range`) and `finish` are not: creating a loan chooses its `final`, and `finish` assumes it equals `current`, so neither is a function of its arguments. The argument that borrowing is sound uses OxCaml's existing modes: uniqueness makes the chain linear, so a prophecy is resolved at most once; locality keeps a loan inside its callback; ghostliness keeps prophecies out of running code. [`borrows-and-slices.md`](src:design-docs/borrows-and-slices.md) has the design.

stops.title: A client proof
stops.text: The client copies an immutable array into an owner with `Owned_array.of_iarray`, sorts it with either operation, and freezes it again with `into_iarray`. The refined result, stated with `Model.of_iarray`, follows from the three contracts with no proof code. The rest of the file runs this on fixed inputs, 129 random lists and four lists of 8,192 elements, and compares both results with `List.sort`. On a runtime configured without `--enable-multidomain`, `Domain.recommended_domain_count ()` is 1, so `parallel_sort_array` never starts a domain in these runs.

stops.title: A rejected sort that only resolves its prophecy
stops.from: (* A sort that leaves its slice unchanged keeps the elements
stops.text: This function takes erased snapshots of `current` and `final`, then calls `Slice.finish` without writing. `finish` gives `final s === current s`, so the checker proves the permutation claim in the body, and it reports a counterexample at the claimed `sorted (final s)`. The same expect test, compiled against the interfaces with `-principal`, rejects a slice overwritten before `sort` that claims a permutation of the original, a `total` function calling `parallel_sort_array` or the borrowing `sort`, and a write inside `ghost_ (...)`. The last is caught by uniqueness: inside `ghost_` the slice is aliased, so `Slice.set` cannot consume it. [`borrow_partial.ml`](src:testsuite/tests/vox/borrow_partial.ml) checks that `ghost_`, lemmas and `total` functions reject `finish` and `with_mut` by their totality.

stops.title: The sequential recursion: sort the children's prophecies
stops.text: Before this point `partition_middle` swaps the middle element to the end and runs Lomuto's `partition`, whose contract keeps `final r.state === final s`: partitioning rewrites `current` and passes the caller's prophecy along. `Slice.split3` then lends the slice as three fresh loans (left, pivot, right), each with its own prophecy. The callback records their `final`s before sorting them, which is legitimate because they are values the loans will have at the end. The recursive calls establish `sorted` and `permutation` of those finals, `Slice.finish middle` resolves the pivot, and `Quicksort_model.glue_partition` proves `post` of the three. `split3`'s contract turns that into a fact about `current state`, and the final `Slice.finish state` resolves the caller's own prophecy; the recursion, through a callback, is checked by `[@@decreases size]`. `sort_sized` is still not `total`, since `split3` and `finish` are not.

stops.title: The total recursion on owned pieces
stops.text: `sort_array` needs no loan. `partition_middle_array` is the same Lomuto partition written with `Owned_array.get` and `Owned_array.swap`, which take the owner and return it. `split_partition` cuts the result into three owners of adjacent ranges with `Owned_array.split_at`, without copying, and `join_partition` appends them again, in place, and proves the whole sorted with `glue_partition`. Every operation takes the owner uniquely and returns its successor, so the function can be read as a pure function of the array's contents, and it is `total`. `Owned_array.append` is total only below `Borrow.max_length ()` elements, where its copying path cannot raise; the contract carries the lengths needed to prove that, starting from `Owned_array.length`, which bounds every owner by `max_length ()`.

stops.title: A fork/join with an ordinary polymorphic type
stops.from: (** [fork_join left right] runs [left] in a new domain
stops.text: `fork_join` mentions no refinement, array or ownership. The thunks are `portable once`, so they capture no unsynchronized state and run once, and their results are `unique`. Vox needs no rule for parallelism here: instantiating `'a` and `'b` at refined types carries each side's proof across the join, as a type argument. `portable` thunks are global, so they cannot capture a borrowed slice, which is `local` to its borrow; that is why the parallel sort works on owned arrays. The implementation, [`vox_parallel.ml`](src:verification/library/vox_parallel.ml), is trusted; see [stop 10](tour:quicksort/10).

stops.title: The parallel recursion on owned pieces
stops.text: `sort_owned` partitions and splits as `sort_array` does. `left_before` and `right_before` are erased snapshots, `sort_left` and `sort_right` annotate their results with refined types, and `fork_join` is instantiated at those types. A domain is started only when both sides have at least `cutoff` elements; otherwise the sides are sorted in turn, each with the whole domain budget. After the join, `join_partition` rejoins the adjacent pieces in place and proves the whole sorted. The refined types also carry each side's length, which `join_partition` needs for `append`'s precondition. `sort_owned` has no `[@@decreases]` and is not total: `fork_join` is not.

stops.title: Trusted: the borrow transitions built into the checker
stops.text: The slice operations above are verified OCaml over private `Raw` externals in [`borrow.ml`](src:verification/library/borrow.ml), implemented in [`runtime/borrow.c`](src:runtime/borrow.c). The checker's knowledge of them has two sources: the refinements on those `external` declarations, and these fixed equations in `normal_borrow_transition`. `open` ties the loan's `final` to its frame, `restore` sets the owner's contents to the frame's final, `split` and `recombine` pass children's finals to the parent's `current`, and `finish` equates `final` and `current`. `open`, `split` and `finish` are the transitions whose `Raw` externals are not `total`. These equations are assumed: nothing proves them against the C code, and they are part of the checker's trusted base.

stops.title: Trusted: owned pieces and the join
stops.text: `Owned_array.get`, `set`, `split_at` and `append` are externals whose refinements (`Model.at`, `Model.set`, `Model.take`, `Model.drop`, `Model.append`) the checker assumes. `caml_borrow_owned_append` joins two adjacent ranges of one backing array without copying and copies any other pair; the copy raises above `max_length ()` elements, which `append`'s precondition excludes. The bound that makes the precondition provable, that no owner is longer than `max_length ()`, is assumed on `Raw.owned_length`. This is sound because owners are unique: the live owners of one array cover disjoint ranges of one OCaml array. [`vox_parallel.ml`](src:verification/library/vox_parallel.ml) is also trusted: it spawns with the mode-checked `Domain.Safe.spawn`, joins before returning or re-raising, and applies `Obj.magic_unique` to the joined result, which `Domain.join` returns `aliased`. Finally, `quicksort.ml` declares integer division as a `@@ total` `external` of `%divint` whose divisor is refined to be nonzero; callers prove that refinement, the checker assumes the declared totality, and the declaration silences warning 228, `trusted-external`.

stops.title: Checked: the sort runs no proof code
stops.text: [`collections_boundary.ml`](src:testsuite/tests/vox/collections_boundary.ml) compiles `quicksort.ml` with `-dlambda`, compiles the quicksort client against the public interfaces only, and runs it. This program then reads the Lambda dump and requires that the bodies of the sorts, partitions and the owned-array `split_partition` and `join_partition` mention neither `Quicksort_model`, `Vox_int_sequence` nor `Vox_sequence`, nor the projections `caml_borrow_current`, `caml_borrow_final` and `caml_borrow_contents`. The check is textual. Erasure does not remove the run-time cost of the library: every `get` and `set` on a slice or an owned array is a C call that checks the index again.
